name: Kartagener syndrome
aliases: primary ciliary dyskinesia with situs inversus totalis

reference.source: ERS/ATS primary ciliary dyskinesia guidance and respiratory genetics texts
clinicalPearls: Recognised by the classic triad of chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, and situs inversus totalis
It is the subset of primary ciliary dyskinesia in which randomisation of embryonic laterality has produced complete mirror-image organ arrangement
Dextrocardia on examination or chest radiograph in a patient with chronic respiratory symptoms should prompt evaluation for the syndrome
Features overlap with primary ciliary dyskinesia generally, including lifelong wet cough, recurrent otitis media, and neonatal respiratory distress in a term infant
Nasal nitric oxide is characteristically low, and diagnosis is confirmed with ciliary video microscopy, electron microscopy, and genetic testing
Fertility is often impaired in both sexes because sperm flagella and fallopian tube cilia share the affected axonemal structures
Management mirrors that of primary ciliary dyskinesia, centring on airway clearance and prompt treatment of infective exacerbations
reference.pathophysiology: Kartagener syndrome is a form of primary ciliary dyskinesia, an autosomal recessive disorder in which mutations affecting motile ciliary components (such as the dynein arms) impair coordinated ciliary beating. Failure of mucociliary clearance leads to chronic retention of secretions with recurrent sinopulmonary infection and progressive bronchiectasis. Because embryonic nodal cilia also fail to establish normal left-right asymmetry, laterality is randomised and roughly half of affected individuals develop complete situs inversus, defining the Kartagener phenotype.
additionalDifferentials: Primary ciliary dyskinesia without situs inversus
Primary immunodeficiency with recurrent sinopulmonary infection
Isolated situs inversus without ciliary disease
Heterotaxy syndromes with complex congenital heart disease
additionalInvestigations: Chest radiograph and imaging demonstrating dextrocardia and situs inversus
High-speed video microscopy of ciliary beat
Transmission electron microscopy of ciliary ultrastructure
Genetic testing for primary ciliary dyskinesia genes
High-resolution chest imaging and sputum microbiology to assess bronchiectasis
redFlags: Progressive bronchiectasis with declining lung function
Recurrent isolation of Pseudomonas or non-tuberculous mycobacteria
Associated complex congenital heart disease in heterotaxy
reference.prognosis: With early diagnosis and consistent airway clearance many patients maintain reasonable lung function, but chronic infection can cause progressive bronchiectasis; the situs inversus itself is usually of little functional consequence unless accompanied by cardiac anomalies.
pitfalls: Assuming isolated situs inversus is benign and missing the underlying ciliary disorder
Delaying diagnosis by attributing chronic wet cough to recurrent infection or asthma
Relying on ultrastructure alone, which can be normal in some genetic subtypes
references: European Respiratory Society statement on primary ciliary dyskinesia
management: Perform daily airway clearance with chest physiotherapy and mucoactive measures to compensate for defective mucociliary clearance
Treat sinopulmonary exacerbations with prompt, often prolonged antibiotics guided by sputum microbiology
Manage chronic sinusitis and recurrent otitis media, with hearing support and ENT input
Surveil lung function and bronchiectasis with high-resolution imaging and immunise against respiratory pathogens
Provide fertility counselling and assisted-reproduction referral given impaired sperm and fallopian tube ciliary function
Offer genetic counselling for this autosomal recessive condition and coordinate multidisciplinary respiratory, ENT and genetics care
